questions.q: The editorial uses an onion to picture “deconditioning.” What does the image convey?
options: Learning always brings tears
Not quite. The article says: Society’s influences cover our pure nature like layers, to be peeled away one by one.
The mind has no centre at all
Not quite. The article says: Society’s influences cover our pure nature like layers, to be peeled away one by one.
Each person has many personalities
Not quite. The article says: Society’s influences cover our pure nature like layers, to be peeled away one by one.
Society’s influences cover our pure nature like layers, to be peeled away one by one
Yes. Until the original nature is uncovered.
questions.rationale: “This conditioning is like a series of coverings over our true nature, similar to the peels of an onion. Deconditioning is a process… of these layers, one by one, until the true, pure nature is uncovered.”

questions.q: According to the editorial, in which two ways can a person be deconditioned?
options: By accepting others’ harsh criticism with an open mind, or by examining himself just as strictly
Right. “Hammering” from outside or from within.
By travel abroad, or by long solitude
Not quite. The article says: By accepting others’ harsh criticism with an open mind, or by examining himself just as strictly.
By changing friends, or by changing work
Not quite. The article says: By accepting others’ harsh criticism with an open mind, or by examining himself just as strictly.
By reading widely, or by fasting
Not quite. The article says: By accepting others’ harsh criticism with an open mind, or by examining himself just as strictly.
questions.rationale: “Either one accepts the ‘hammering’ of others or one becomes one’s own worst critic by ‘self-hammering’.”

questions.q: In a time of sharp religious disputes, people rallied round Rabia Basri. What, according to the article, did she emphasise?
options: Debate until one side won
Not quite. The article says: Pure love of God, which made their differences seem small.
Strict rules for each group
Not quite. The article says: Pure love of God, which made their differences seem small.
Withdrawal from all society
Not quite. The article says: Pure love of God, which made their differences seem small.
Pure love of God, which made their differences seem small
Well read. Her spiritual character drew people together.
questions.rationale: “She laid emphasis on pure divine love, which alone could minimize all these differences.”

questions.q: The universe is unimaginably vast, yet works in complete harmony. What does the article conclude from this?
options: Its harmony is only apparent
Not quite. The article says: It is governed by a single, all-powerful Creator – otherwise it would fall into chaos.
It is too large to have any order
Not quite. The article says: It is governed by a single, all-powerful Creator – otherwise it would fall into chaos.
It is governed by a single, all-powerful Creator – otherwise it would fall into chaos
Yes. The smallest deviation would upset the whole.
Its parts are independent of one another
Not quite. The article says: It is governed by a single, all-powerful Creator – otherwise it would fall into chaos.
questions.rationale: “This perfect harmony in the universe is a proof that it is functioning under an All-Powerful Creator. Had this not been so, the whole universe would be reduced to ultimate chaos.”

questions.q: A ship approaching the shore shows its mast first and then its hull. What does the article use this to show?
options: That ships were once built with tall masts
Not quite. The article says: That discoveries come from thinking about what we see – here, that the earth is not flat.
That eyesight weakens with distance
Not quite. The article says: That discoveries come from thinking about what we see – here, that the earth is not flat.
That the sea is higher far from land
Not quite. The article says: That discoveries come from thinking about what we see – here, that the earth is not flat.
That discoveries come from thinking about what we see – here, that the earth is not flat
Correct. Like Newton and the falling apple.
questions.rationale: “If the earth was flat, the entire ship would have appeared in the distance… The truth is that all discoveries are made solely by thinking.”

questions.q: “Dogs may bark, but the elephant goes on.” What principle of right thinking does the saying illustrate?
options: Noise always signals danger
Not quite. The article says: Do not be drawn into every provocation; keep to your own constructive course.
Do not be drawn into every provocation; keep to your own constructive course
Right. Avoidance is the better option, not cowardice.
The strong may ignore the law
Not quite. The article says: Do not be drawn into every provocation; keep to your own constructive course.
Small people should stay silent
Not quite. The article says: Do not be drawn into every provocation; keep to your own constructive course.
questions.rationale: “Instead of wasting your time being provoked into fighting, you should stick to the path of positive action and avoid negative action.”

questions.q: Everyone has his own idea of what is ideal. What does the article call the only practical solution in dealing with others?
options: Letting the strongest decide
Not quite. The article says: A policy of adjustment.
Living entirely alone
Not quite. The article says: A policy of adjustment.
Persuading everyone to agree
Not quite. The article says: A policy of adjustment.
A policy of adjustment
Well reasoned. Insisting on one’s personal ideal leads to conflict.
questions.rationale: “The achievement of the personal ideal is impossible. The only practical solution is to adopt the policy of adjustment with others.”

questions.q: Khadija had been the wealthiest lady of Makkah. What did she do during the years when the believers were driven out to live in tents?
options: She remained in her house in the city
Not quite. The article says: She chose to stay with the Prophet and bore hunger and hardship patiently, without complaint.
She asked her relatives to end the ban
Not quite. The article says: She chose to stay with the Prophet and bore hunger and hardship patiently, without complaint.
She travelled to another land
Not quite. The article says: She chose to stay with the Prophet and bore hunger and hardship patiently, without complaint.
She chose to stay with the Prophet and bore hunger and hardship patiently, without complaint
Yes. Her wealth had already been given to the cause.
questions.rationale: “Khadija could have stayed on in Makkah. But she chose to stay with the Prophet in these times of trial and difficulty… But she did not complain.”

questions.q: A man moved a full-grown tree into his courtyard to save time, and it withered. What did he say he had learned?
options: “Courtyards are too small for trees”
Not quite. The article says: “I am in a hurry, but God isn’t” – nature works by gradual growth, not sudden leaps.
“Large trees need more water”
Not quite. The article says: “I am in a hurry, but God isn’t” – nature works by gradual growth, not sudden leaps.
“Labourers cannot be trusted”
Not quite. The article says: “I am in a hurry, but God isn’t” – nature works by gradual growth, not sudden leaps.
“I am in a hurry, but God isn’t” – nature works by gradual growth, not sudden leaps
Exactly. Realism is the root of patience.
questions.rationale: “‘I am in a hurry, but God isn’t.’ This story informs us about the law of nature, which is based on gradual development and not on sudden leaps.”

questions.q: In a factory the Maulana saw a flywheel reverse its direction within seconds. What did it suggest to him about anger?
options: If a machine can change direction so quickly, a person can train himself to switch from rage to silence at once
Well read. Silence lets anger subside.
That anger should be released quickly
Not quite. The article says: If a machine can change direction so quickly, a person can train himself to switch from rage to silence at once.
That factories are stressful places
Not quite. The article says: If a machine can change direction so quickly, a person can train himself to switch from rage to silence at once.
That machines are superior to men
Not quite. The article says: If a machine can change direction so quickly, a person can train himself to switch from rage to silence at once.
questions.rationale: “When matter (or machine) has the quality to change its direction within seconds, then a human being should have this ability manifold.”
